about.title: Winters Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Winters is a small town, but its roads carry real traffic — especially along E Grant Avenue and County Road 89 near Niemann Street, where public records show collisions cluster on Friday mornings between 7 and 9 a.m. In 2025, Winters logged 5 injury collisions and 6 people hurt, numbers that remind us these crashes happen to real neighbors, commuters, and farmworkers passing through Yolo County. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the process of dealing with insurance adjusters, medical bills, and lost wages can feel overwhelming on top of recovery. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured people in Winters with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, handle communications with insurers, and help protect your rights while you focus on healing. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Winters Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file suit, but claims against a government entity — like a road defect on a county-maintained stretch of County Road 89 — can require a claim in as little as six months. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Protections
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, though your recovery may be reduced by your share of fault. An independent attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly shifted onto you during settlement talks.

items.title: No Recorded Statement Needed Yet
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly after a crash, but you're not required to give one before speaking with an attorney. Protecting what you say — and preserving evidence like photos or witness contacts — can matter more than people expect.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Winters?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If the crash involved a government-maintained road, such as a county road near Niemann Street, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. Because these timelines vary, it helps to get guidance early rather than waiting.

items.question: Will my case be affected if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than being barred entirely.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: You're not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often wise to speak with an attorney first. Statements made early on, especially before you know the full extent of your injuries, can sometimes be used against you later. An independent attorney can help you understand what to say and when.
